name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that only appears when keyboard focus arrives. This guarantees keyboard users bypass repetitive blocks in one jump, fixing the most common navigation failure without cluttering the visual design. The trade-off is a tiny extra DOM node and a focused state style, both negligible compared to the universal benefit.

name: Reader
text: Risk: Hiding the skip link until first tab press means screen-reader users who rely on virtual cursors never see it—so they still slog through blocks. Better: always show the skip link but style it off-screen until focus arrives. Settle with testing: run a screen-reader user through both versions and measure time to reach main content.

name: Ramp
text:
We should always show the skip link but style it off-screen until focus arrives, as this ensures screen-reader users can discover it through their virtual cursors. This approach provides a better experience for users relying on assistive technologies, as they can choose to use the skip link if needed. The trade-off is a slightly more complex CSS rule to position the link off-screen, but this is a worthwhile compromise for the improved accessibility. By doing so, we guarantee that all users, including those with disabilities, can efficiently navigate our pages.

name: Reader
text: Risk: Always-showing skip links clutter the top of the page for sighted users who never need them, especially on mobile where vertical space is tight. Better: keep the on-focus reveal but test with screen-reader users who navigate by virtual cursor—if they still miss it, add a brief ARIA live announcement when the link appears. Settle with a quick A/B test measured by task completion time for keyboard-only and screen-reader users.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **bold, full-width skip bar** that’s always visible but styled off-screen until focus arrives; test with screen-reader users navigating by virtual cursor—if they still miss it, add a brief ARIA live announcement on first tab press. Result: skip link works for all users. Owner: Ramp.
